chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Wahb, from al-Husayn ibn Abd Allah ibn Damrah, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), that he said: He elevated the narration to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).

That he passed by the hoarders (al-muhtakirin) and ordered that their hoarding be removed and brought to the centers of the markets and where the eyes could see them. It was said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'If you had fixed their prices (qawwamta 'alayhim)?' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became angry until the anger was evident on his face, and he said, 'I will fix their prices? No, the price (al-si'r) is to Allah; He raises it when He wills and lowers it when He wills.'

key_terms.الْمُحْتَكِرِينَ: Hoarders, those who buy up goods to create scarcity

ai.seo_question: What is the Prophet's stance on price fixing (ta'sir) versus divine decree in Islamic economics?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia understanding of *al-si'r* (price fixation) as a natural economic phenomenon driven by market forces rather than a direct divine decree, a view supported by the Prophet's anger at the suggestion of artificial control. It highlights the distinction between the Prophet's role in managing market practices, such as exposing hoarded goods to public view, and God's ultimate sovereignty over supply and demand. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between *si'r* (natural price fluctuation) and *tas'ir* (government-imposed price fixing).
